newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's monetary base contracts 4.5 pct in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's monetary base contracts 4.5 pct in Nov.

text.p: Brazil's monetary base as measured by daily averages contracted 4.5 percent in November, compared to an expansion of 3.0 percent in November of last year, the Central Bank said.
November's figure brings the accumulated 12-month expansion to 0.7 percent, down from October's 12-month accumulated figure of 8.6 percent, the bank said in a statement.
The bank also said net public sector debt in October stood at 260.3 billion reais, or 34.2 percent of gross domestic product, versus 256.6 billion reais, or 33.9 percent of GDP, in September.
Net internal debt in October was 227.3 billion reais or 29.9 percent of GDP, while net external debt was 33 billion reais, or 4.3 percent of GDP, the bank said.

The public sector operational deficit, which includes expenditures for interest payments on government debt, represented 3.98 percent of GDP in the January-October period, compared with 3.89 percent in the January-September period.

In the January-October period, the federal government and the Central Bank posted an operational deficit of 1.69 percent of GDP; the states and municipalities, 2.18 percent of GDP; and state firms, 0.11 percent of GDP.

In primary terms, which excludes expenditures on interest payments, the public sector showed a surplus of 0.02 percent of GDP through October, compared with a primary deficit of 0.06 percent of GDP up to September, the bank said.
According to daily averages, the monetary base in October was 16.859 billion reais, compared with 17.653 billion reais in September, the bank said.

Brazil's public sector borrowing requirement, encompassing federal, state and municipal governments, the Central Bank and state companies from January through October was 37.443 billion reais, or 6.01 percent of GDP, compared with a deficit of 33.831 billion reais or 6.06 percent of GDP for the January-September period.
